rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that two sons learned their mother was condemned for burying a child alive in pre-Islamic times despite her kindness; the Prophet said his mother was with theirs.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: جاء ابنا مليكة إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالا إن أمنا [كانت] (7) تكرم الزوج

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: The Prophet identified the praised station with his unique standing on the Day of Resurrection, after Abraham is first clothed, where earlier and later people envy him.
rows.anchor: فأقوم عن يمينه مقاما لا يقومه أحد، فيغبطني فيه الأولون والآخرون

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: The report says a channel from al-Kawthar opens to the Basin; its bed is musk, its gravel is described as التوم, and gold rods and jewel-like fruits grow there.
rows.anchor: ويفتح نهر (1) من الكوثر إلى الحوض

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: The Kawthar water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey; whoever drinks once never thirsts again, while the deprived person is never quenched.
rows.anchor: وماؤه أشد بياضا من اللبن، وأحلى من العسل، من شرب منه شربة (3) لا يظمأ بعده

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that all people gather on one plain, hear the caller and see across it, while the approaching sun brings unbearable distress and they seek an intercessor, beginning with Adam.
rows.anchor: يجمع الله الأولين والآخرين في صعيد واحد، يسمعهم الداعي وينفذهم البصر، وتدنو الشمس

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Adam refuses to intercede because he disobeyed God's prohibition concerning the tree and directs the people to Noah.
rows.anchor: وإنه نهاني عن الشجرة فعصيته، نفسي، نفسي، نفسي! اذهبوا إلى غيري، اذهبوا إلى نوح

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Noah refuses because he had a supplication against his people and sends the people to Abraham.
rows.anchor: وإنه كانت لي دعوة (4) على قومي، نفسي، نفسي، نفسي! اذهبوا إلى غيري، اذهبوا إلى إبراهيم.

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abraham declines on account of the lies he recalls and sends the people to Moses.
rows.anchor: فذكر كذباته نفسي، نفسي، نفسي [اذهبوا إلى غيري] (6) اذهبوا إلى موسى.

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Moses refuses because he killed someone without being commanded to do so and directs them to Jesus.
rows.anchor: وإني قتلت نفسا لم أومر بقتلها، نفسي، نفسي، نفسي، اذهبوا إلى غيري، اذهبوا إلى عيسى

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Jesus recalls no sin, but says God is angrier than ever and sends the people to Muhammad for intercession.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكر ذنبا، اذهبوا إلى غيري، اذهبوا إلى محمد

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Muhammad prostrates beneath the Throne, receives inspired praises, is told to ask and intercede, and repeatedly asks for his community; some enter Paradise without reckoning through its right gate.
rows.anchor: فأقوم فآتي تحت العرش، فأقع ساجدا لربي، عز وجل، ثم يفتح الله علي، ويلهمني من محامده

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet says he is the master of Adam's descendants, the first whose grave opens, the first intercessor, and the first whose intercession is accepted.
rows.anchor: أنا سيد ولد آدم يوم القيامة، وأول من ينشق عنه القبر، وأول شافع، وأول مشفع

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet identifies the praised station as the intercession he makes for his community.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: {عسى أن يبعثك ربك مقاما محمودا}

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: In a report the author explicitly calls mursal, the earth is spread flat, the Prophet is summoned first with Gabriel at the Merciful's right, then intercedes for God's worshippers across the earth; this is the praised station.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن الحسين قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إذا كان يوم القيامة، مد الله الأرض مد الأديم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Muhammad was in Mecca when commanded to migrate, and this prayer was then revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة ثم أمر بالهجرة، فأنزل الله

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the requested supporting authority as God's promise to transfer Persian and Roman kingship and power to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن البصري في تفسيرها: وعده ربه لينزعن ملك فارس، وعز (4) فارس، وليجعلنه له، وملك الروم،

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Muhammad knew the mission required authority to uphold scripture, God's limits and religion; political authority is mercy that restrains the strong from preying on the weak.
rows.anchor: فسأل سلطانا نصيرا لكتاب الله، ولحدود الله، ولفرائض الله، ولإقامة دين الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets the supporting authority as a clear proof.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: {سلطانا نصيرا} حجة بينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers Hasan's and Qatada's political-authority view: truth needs power against its enemies; he links this to the sending of iron and the saying that authority restrains where the Quran does not.
rows.anchor: واختار ابن جرير قول الحسن وقتادة، وهو الأرجح؛ لأنه لا بد مع الحق من قهر لمن عاداه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse threatens Quraysh: God's Quran, faith and beneficial knowledge have come as undeniable truth, while their falsehood has perished because falsehood cannot endure beside truth.
rows.anchor: تهديد ووعيد لكفار قريش؛ فإنه قد جاءهم من الله الحق الذي لا مرية فيه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that at the conquest of Mecca the Prophet struck the 360 idols around the Kaaba with a stick and recited that truth had come and falsehood vanished.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: دخل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مكة وحول البيت ستون وثلاثمائة نصب

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir reports that the Prophet ordered the 360 idols worshipped around the Kaaba to fall face-first and recited the verse.
rows.anchor: عن جابر رضي الله عنه، قال: دخلنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مكة، وحول البيت ثلاثمائة وستون صنما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran heals heart-diseases such as doubt, hypocrisy, associating partners and deviation, and grants believers faith, wisdom and desire for good; this benefit belongs to those who believe, affirm and follow it.
rows.anchor: يذهب ما في القلوب من أمراض، من شك ونفاق، وشرك وزيغ وميل، فالقرآن يشفي من ذلك كله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says believers benefit from the Quran by retaining and understanding it, while wrongdoers neither benefit nor preserve or comprehend it; the fault lies with them, not the Quran.
rows.anchor: إذا سمعه المؤمن انتفع به وحفظه ووعاه {ولا يزيد الظالمين إلا خسارا} إنه لا ينتفع به ولا يحفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings generally turn from worship and turn away when God grants wealth, health, provision, victory or what they desire, except those God protects.
rows.anchor: إذا أنعم الله عليه بمال وعافية، وفتح ورزق ونصر، ونال ما يريد، أعرض عن طاعة الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses turning aside as moving away from God.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: بعد عنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When hardship and calamities touch a person, he despairs of future good; Ibn Kathir links this to the contrast in Hud 10–11 between boastful joy and the patience of the righteous.
rows.anchor: وبأنه إذا مسه الشر -وهو المصائب والحوادث والنوائب - {كان يئوسا} أي: قنط أن يعود يحصل له

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains each person acting according to his own side or way.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: على ناحيته

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses each person's manner as his disposition and nature.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: على حدته وطبيعته

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets each person's manner as his intention.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: على نيته

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets each person's manner as his religion; Ibn Kathir says the reported meanings are close.
rows.anchor:
وقال ابن زيد: دينه.
وكل هذه الأقوال متقاربة في المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse warns the polytheists that each acts in his own manner; God knows who is better guided and will repay every worker, since nothing is hidden from him.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية -والله أعلم -تهديد للمشركين ووعيد لهم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Jews in Medina asked Muhammad about the spirit; revelation then instructed him to say that it belongs to God's command and human knowledge is slight.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله -هو ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه -قال: كنت أمشي مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في حرث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report's apparent Medina setting would make the verse Medinan despite the Meccan surah; Ibn Kathir suggests it may have been revealed again there or that an earlier verse was given as the answer.
rows.anchor: وهذا السياق يقتضي (8) فيما يظهر بادي الرأي: أن هذه الآية مدنية، وأنها إنما نزلت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Quraysh asked Jews what to ask Muhammad, and the Jews proposed the spirit; after his answer they boasted of the Torah, and God revealed that even the seas cannot exhaust his words.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قالت قريش ليهود: أعطونا شيئا نسأل عنه هذا الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir takes the Quraysh-to-Jews report as evidence for a Meccan revelation, despite the Medina setting in Ibn Masud's report.
rows.anchor: ومما يدل على نزول هذه الآية بمكة ما قال الإمام أحمد

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima reports that the People of the Book objected that they possessed the Torah and wisdom; the response was that knowledge saving them from Hell is much yet little relative to God's knowledge.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: سأل أهل الكتاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الروح

rows.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
rows.claim: Ata ibn Yasar reports that the verse was revealed in Mecca; after migration Jewish scholars ask whether it means them or Muhammad's people, and he replies that it includes them all and their knowledge is little before God.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار قال: نزلت بمكة: {وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Awfi transmits Ibn Abbas's view that the spirit means human souls; Jews asked how a soul from God could be punished, and Gabriel brought the answer, provoking their claim that he was their enemy.
rows.anchor: قال العوفي، عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ويسألونك عن الروح} الآية، وذلك أن اليهود قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the spirit here is Gabriel and that Ibn Abbas used to conceal this interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالروح هاهنا: جبريل. قاله قتادة، قال: وكان ابن عباس يكتمه.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report through Ali ibn Talha attributes to Ibn Abbas the view that the spirit is an angel; another report describes an immense angel able to swallow the heavens and earth in one bite, which Ibn Kathir grades strange and munkar.
rows.anchor: قال (4) علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس قوله: {ويسألونك عن الروح} يقول: الروح: ملك.

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali is reported to describe the spirit as an angel with 70,000 faces, tongues and languages, whose glorifications each create an angel; Ibn Kathir calls the report strange and wondrous.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب، رضي الله عنه، أنه قال في قوله: {ويسألونك عن الروح} قال: هو ملك من الملائكة، له سبعون ألف وجه

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli also transmits from Ali a description of an angel with 100,000 heads, faces, mouths and tongues praising God in varied languages.
rows.anchor: قال السهيلي: روي عن علي أنه قال: هو ملك، له مائة ألف رأس، لكل رأس مائة ألف وجه،

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli reports a view that the spirit is a group of angels in human form.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بذلك: طائفة من الملائكة على صور بني آدم

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli reports a group that sees angels while angels do not see them, standing to angels as angels stand to human beings.
rows.anchor: وقيل: طائفة يرون الملائكة ولا تراهم (1) فهم للملائكة كالملائكة لبني آدم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spirit is of God's affair, meaning a matter reserved to his knowledge; people receive only a little of what God knows, and this question was not disclosed to them.
rows.anchor: أي: من شأنه، ومما استأثر بعلمه دونكم؛ ولهذا قال: {وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bird's sip from the sea illustrates that Moses, Khidr and all creatures know only an infinitesimal amount beside God's knowledge.
rows.anchor: ما علمي وعلمك وعلم الخلائق في علم الله إلا كما أخذ هذا العصفور من هذا البحر

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli says either the question was left unanswered because it was asked in obstinacy, or it was answered as an invitation to follow divine law, since reason and philosophy cannot reveal the spirit; Ibn Kathir finds the latter reasoning questionable.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أجابهم، وعول السهيلي على أن المراد بقوله: {قل الروح من أمر ربي} أي: من شرعه

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli describes the spirit as a subtle substance flowing through the body like water through a tree; joined to the body it becomes the soul, acquiring praiseworthy or blameworthy qualities, and soul and spirit are one aspectually, not wholly. Ibn Kathir calls this a good account.
rows.anchor: فحاصل ما يقول أن الروح أصل النفس ومادتها، والنفس مركبة منها ومن اتصالها بالبدن، فهي هي من وجه لا من كل وجه (4)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that scholars have written on the spirit's nature and rulings, and singles out Hafiz Ibn Manda's book as among the best discussions, which he had heard.
rows.anchor: ومن أحسن من تكلم على ذلك الحافظ ابن منده، في كتاب سمعناه في: الروح (5)

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says a red wind from Syria will come at the end of time, erasing every Quran verse from people's codices and hearts; he recited this verse.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود، رضي الله عنه: يطرق الناس ريح حمراء -يعني في آخر الزمان -من قبل الشام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reminds Muhammad that the revealed Quran is a great favor, and that no combination of humans and jinn, even cooperating, can produce its like because created speech cannot match the Creator.
rows.anchor: أنه لو اجتمعت الإنس والجن كلهم، واتفقوا (1) على أن يأتوا بمثل ما أنزله على رسوله،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is cited for a report that the challenge verse came after a group of Jews told Muhammad they could bring something like his revelation; Ibn Kathir questions this because the surah is Meccan and its context concerns Quraysh.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: إن هذه الآية نزلت في نفر من اليهود، جاءوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has varied examples and proofs throughout the Quran, clarifying and expanding the truth, yet most people refuse it and persist in denial.
rows.anchor: أي: بينا لهم الحجج والبراهين القاطعة، ووضحنا لهم الحق وشرحناه وبسطناه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas's report describes Quraysh leaders summoning Muhammad to blame his division of the community and insulting his message; they offer wealth, rank, kingship or treatment if he is possessed, while he says he was sent as a messenger and will patiently await God's judgment.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس: أن عتبة وشيبة ابني ربيعة، وأبا سفيان بن حرب، ورجلا من بني عبد الدار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Muhammad rejects their offers of wealth, social standing and kingship, explaining that he was sent as a messenger rather than to seek their money, status or rule.
rows.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ما بي ما تقولون، ما جئتكم بما جئتكم به أطلب أموالكم، ولا الشرف فيكم، ولا الملك عليكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Quraysh next demand an angel to confirm Muhammad, gardens, treasures and gold palaces, or that the sky fall; Muhammad repeatedly says he was sent only to warn and give good news, and that such acts belong to God.
rows.anchor: فخذ لنفسك، فاسأل ربك أن يبعث ملكا يصدقك بما تقول (1) ويراجعنا عنك، وتسأله فيجعل لك جنانا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The leaders reject the name al-Rahman, accuse a man in Yamama of teaching Muhammad, and demand that God and the angels appear before them.
rows.anchor: فقد بلغنا أنه إنما يعلمك هذا رجل باليمامة، يقال له: الرحمن

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي أمية
rows.claim: Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayya says he will never believe unless Muhammad climbs a visible ladder to heaven and returns with a written revelation and four witnessing angels; he doubts he would believe even then.
rows.anchor: يا محمد، عرض عليك قومك ما عرضوا، فلم تقبله منهم، ثم سألوك لأنفسهم أمورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knew the gathering sought obstinate disbelief, not guidance, so Muhammad chose the offered door of repentance and mercy rather than extraordinary signs followed by an unprecedented punishment.
rows.anchor: لو (7) علم الله منهم أنهم يسألون ذلك استرشادا لأجيبوا إليه، ولكن علم أنهم إنما يطلبون ذلك كفرا وعنادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet returned to his family sorrowful and grieved by the Meccans' rejection, having hoped that their summons meant they were ready for guidance.
rows.anchor: وانصرف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى أهله حزينا أسفا لما فاته، مما كان طمع فيه من قومه حين دعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A yanbu is a flowing spring; the Meccans demanded springs at various places in the Hijaz, an easy feat for God, but God knew signs would not guide those already fixed in rejection.
rows.anchor: الينبوع: العين الجارية، سألوه أن يجري لهم عينا معينا في أرض الحجاز هاهنا وهاهنا، وذلك (2) سهل يسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They demand that the sky fall in pieces immediately, though Muhammad had described its splitting and hanging edges at the Resurrection; Ibn Kathir links their demand to earlier challenges for heavenly punishment.
rows.anchor: أي: أنك وعدتنا أن يوم القيامة تنشق فيه السماء وتهي، وتدلى أطرافها، فعجل ذلك في الدنيا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a prophet of mercy, Muhammad asked that they be given respite so descendants might worship God alone; some did convert, including Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayya.
rows.anchor: فسأل إنظارهم وتأجيلهم، لعل الله أن يخرج من أصلابهم من يعبده لا يشرك به شيئا. وكذلك وقع،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatada gloss زُخرف as gold; Ibn Masud's reading makes the phrase explicitly a house of gold.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وقتادة: هو الذهب. وكذلك هو في قراءة ابن مسعود:

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets their requested written revelation as an individual paper from God for each person, placed by that person's head.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: أي مكتوب فيه إلى كل واحد واحد صحيفة: هذا كتاب من الله لفلان بن فلان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God cannot be preempted in his sovereign actions; Muhammad is only a messenger who conveys and advises, leaving the requested signs to God's choice.
rows.anchor: سبحانه وتعالى وتقدس أن يتقدم أحد بين يديه في أمر من أمور سلطانه وملكوته

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: The Prophet says God offered to make Mecca's lowland gold, but he preferred alternating hunger and satiety so he could remember God in need and thank him when full; Tirmidhi calls the report hasan but notes Ali ibn Zayd is weak.
rows.anchor: عن أبي أمامة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "عرض ربي عز وجل ليجعل لي بطحاء مكة ذهبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People repeatedly reject prophets because they are human; God mercifully sends messengers from the recipients' own kind so they can understand, address and learn from them.
rows.anchor: إلا استعجابهم من بعثته (4) البشر رسلا كما قال تعالى: {أكان للناس عجبا أن أوحينا إلى رجل منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If angels inhabited earth at ease, God would send them an angel messenger of their kind; since humans inhabit earth, their messengers are human, as an act of grace and mercy.
rows.anchor: ولو بعث إلى البشر رسولا من الملائكة لما استطاعوا مواجهته ولا الأخذ عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's witness establishes the Prophet's truth; were Muhammad lying about God, God would punish him severely, as in the warning about fabricating revelation.
rows.anchor: فلو كنت كاذبا [عليه] (1) انتقم مني أشد الانتقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows which servants deserve favor, guidance and kindness and which deserve misery, misguidance and deviation.
rows.anchor: أي: عليم بهم بمن يستحق الإنعام والإحسان والهداية، ممن يستحق الشقاء والإضلال (2) والإزاغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's judgment over creation cannot be overturned: whoever he guides is guided, and no protector can guide those he misleads.
rows.anchor: بأنه من يهده فلا مضل له (ومن يضلل فلن تجد لهم أولياء من دونه) أي: يهدونهم

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Asked how people can be gathered on their faces, the Prophet answers that the one who made them walk on their feet can make them walk on their faces; the report is in both Sahih collections.
rows.anchor: يا رسول الله، كيف يحشر (2) الناس على وجوههم؟ قال: "الذي أمشاهم على أرجلهم قادر على أن يمشيهم على وجوههم"

rows.speaker: حذيفة بن أسيد
rows.claim: Abu Dharr transmits that people will be gathered in three groups: mounted, fed and clothed; walking and running; or dragged face-first by angels to the Fire, after mounts are afflicted.
rows.anchor: أن الناس يحشرون على ثلاثة أفواج: فوج راكبين طاعمين كاسين، وفوج (5) يمشون ويسعون،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned are blind, mute and deaf at a stage of the gathering as requital for ignoring truth that way in life, precisely when they most need those faculties.
rows.anchor: وقوله: (عميا) أي: لا يبصرون (وبكما) يعني: لا ينطقون (وصما) : لا يسمعون.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the Fire's abating as becoming calm; Mujahid glosses it as going out, after which God increases its flame, heat and embers.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: سكنت (2) . وقال مجاهد: طفئت (زدناهم سعيرا) أي: لهبا ووهجا وجمرا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment repays rejection of God's proofs and denial of bodily resurrection after decay; creating the heavens and earth proves God can restore human bodies, indeed that is easier for him.
rows.anchor: فاحتج (4) تعالى عليهم، ونبههم على قدرته على ذلك، بأنه خلق السماوات والأرض،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God appointed an undeniable fixed term for resurrection and emergence from the graves; despite the proof, wrongdoers persist in falsehood and disbelief.
rows.anchor: جعل لإعادتهم وإقامتهم من قبورهم أجلا مضروبا ومدة مقدرة لا بد من انقضائها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada explain that people would hoard God's inexhaustible mercy out of fear of poverty and spending it away.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، وقتادة: أي الفقر أي: خشية أن تذهبوها (2)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada gloss قتورا as miserly and withholding.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، وقتادة (3) : أي بخيلا منوعا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings generally show miserliness, anxiety and hoarding unless God guides them; if given a share in God's kingdom, they would give no one even a speck, as another verse says.
rows.anchor: والله تعالى يصف الإنسان من حيث هو، إلا من وفقه الله وهداه؛ فإن البخل والجزع والهلع صفة له،

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet says God's hands remain full and generous; spending day and night does not diminish what is in his possession, as narrated in both Sahih collections.
rows.anchor: يد الله ملأى لا يغيضها نفقة، سحاء الليل والنهار، أرأيتم ما أنفق منذ خلق السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One list of Moses's nine signs is the staff, hand, years of drought, sea, flood, locusts, lice, frogs and blood.
rows.anchor: وهي: العصا، واليد، والسنين (6) ، والبحر، والطوفان (7) ، والجراد، والقمل، والضفادع، والدم، آيات مفصلات.

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kab lists the hand and staff, five signs from al-Araf, the obliteration sign and the stone.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب: هي اليد، والعصا، والخمس في الأعراف، والطمسة والحجر.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrima, al-Shabi and Qatada give the staff, hand, drought years, crop shortage, flood, locusts, lice, frogs and blood; Ibn Kathir calls this clear and strong.
rows.anchor: وقال: ابن عباس أيضا، ومجاهد، وعكرمة والشعبي، وقتادة: هي يده، وعصاه، والسنين، ونقص الثمرات، والطوفان، والجراد

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Hasan counts drought and crop shortage as one sign and makes the ninth sign the staff swallowing what the magicians fabricated.
rows.anchor: وجعل الحسن البصري "السنين ونقص الثمرات" واحدة، وعنده أن التاسعة هي: تلقف العصا ما يأفكون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nine signs were the public proofs witnessed by Pharaoh and Egypt, distinct from later signs given to the Israelites; their rejection shows the Meccan demand for miracles would not produce belief without God's will.
rows.anchor: فكذلك لو أجبنا هؤلاء الذين سألوا منك (2) سألوا، وقالوا: {لن نؤمن لك حتى تفجر لنا من الأرض ينبوعا}

rows.speaker: صفوان بن عسال المرادي
rows.claim: A report has Jews ask about the nine signs; the Prophet answers with commands against idolatry, theft, fornication, murder, sorcery, usury, betraying an innocent person, slander or fleeing battle, and Sabbath-breaking. The Jews testify he is a prophet but fear their people.
rows.anchor: عن صفوان بن عسال المرادي، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال يهودي لصاحبه: اذهب بنا إلى هذا النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although transmitted by several compilers and graded hasan sahih by Tirmidhi, Ibn Kathir finds the report problematic because Abdullah ibn Salama's memory was criticized; the ten commands likely became confused with Moses's nine signs.
rows.anchor: وقال الترمذي: حسن صحيح. وهو حديث مشكل، وعبد الله بن سلمة في حفظه شيء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says Pharaoh knew the signs were clear proofs from the Lord of the heavens and earth; مثبورا can mean destroyed, which Ibn Kathir says encompasses the other glosses.
rows.anchor: أي: حججا وأدلة على صدق ما جئتك به (وإني لأظنك يا فرعون مثبورا) أي: هالكا.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada gloss مثبورا as destroyed.
rows.anchor: قاله مجاهد وقتادة. وقال ابن عباس ملعونا.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses مثبورا as accursed; Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak also gloss it as overcome.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ملعونا. وقال: أيضا هو والضحاك: (مثبورا) أي: مغلوبا.

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: A reading attributed to Ali raises the ت in علمت, while the majority reading opens it as a direct address to Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم برفع التاء من قوله: "علمت" وروي ذلك عن علي بن أبي طالب.

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبعرى
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zibara's verse uses مثبور with the sense of doomed or destroyed.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن الزبعرى: إذ أجاري الشيطان في سنن الغ … ي ومن مال ميله مثبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nine signs are staff, hand, drought years, crop shortage, flood, locusts, lice, frogs and blood; the report listing moral commandments lacks relevance to Pharaoh and likely confused the nine signs with ten commandments.
rows.anchor: ولعل ذينك اليهوديين إنما سألا عن العشر الكلمات، فاشتبه على الراوي بالتسع الآيات، فحصل وهم في ذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh sought to drive the Israelites from the land; God drowned him and his followers, then ordered Israel to settle the land and later gather with its enemies; لفيفا means all together according to Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatada and al-Dahhak.
rows.anchor: وقوله: (فأراد أن يستفزهم من الأرض) أي: يخليهم منها ويزيلهم (8) عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This foretells Muhammad's conquest of Mecca: the Meccans tried to expel him, but God returned the city to him; on the better-known view he took it by force, then pardoned its people generously, paralleling Israel's inheritance of Pharaoh's lands.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا بشارة لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بفتح مكة مع أن السورة نزلت قبل الهجرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatada and al-Dahhak gloss لفيفا as gathered all together.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك: (لفيفا) أي: جميعا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran descended containing truth, including God's knowledge of the rulings, commands and prohibitions he chose to reveal.
rows.anchor: أي: متضمنا للحق، كما قال تعالى: {لكن الله يشهد بما أنزل إليك أنزله بعلمه}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran reached Muhammad protected and preserved, with no adulteration, addition or deletion, carried by the mighty, trustworthy angel obeyed in the highest assembly.
rows.anchor: أي: ووصل إليك -يا محمد -محفوظا محروسا، لم يشب بغيره، ولا زيد فيه ولا نقص منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad was sent as a bearer of glad tidings for obedient believers and a warner to disobedient unbelievers.
rows.anchor: أي: يا محمد {إلا مبشرا} لمن أطاعك من المؤمنين {ونذيرا} لمن عصاك من الكافرين.

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima transmits Ibn Abbas's reading with lightening: the Quran was transferred from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven, then revealed to Muhammad in installments over 23 years as events occurred.
rows.anchor: ثم نزل مفرقا منجما على الوقائع إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في ثلاث وعشرين سنة. قاله عكرمة عن ابن عباس.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also reads the verb with doubling, meaning the Quran was revealed verse by verse, explained clearly, so Muhammad could recite it to people gradually.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا أنه قال {فرقناه} بالتشديد، أي: أنزلناه آية آية، مبينا مفسرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether unbelievers accept the Quran or not, it remains God's true revelation and had been acclaimed in earlier scriptures; the learned among earlier peoples are upright custodians who did not alter their books.
rows.anchor: أي: سواء آمنتم به أم لا فهو حق في نفسه، أنزله الله ونوه بذكره في سالف الأزمان (2) في كتبه المنزلة على رسله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When such learned people hear the Quran, they prostrate on their chins in gratitude that God let them witness the messenger and revealed book.
rows.anchor: إذا يتلى عليهم} هذا القرآن، {يخرون للأذقان} جمع ذقن، وهو أسفل الوجه {سجدا} أي: لله عز وجل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They glorify God and affirm that the promise made through earlier prophets has truly been fulfilled.
rows.anchor: سبحان ربنا إن كان وعد ربنا لمفعولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their weeping expresses submission, faith and acceptance of God's book and messenger; God increases their humility as increased guidance brings faith and submission.
rows.anchor: أي: خضوعا لله عز وجل وإيمانا وتصديقا بكتابه ورسوله، ويزيدهم الله خشوعا، أي: إيمانا وتسليما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, the second ويخرون adds one descriptive quality to another, not a second prostration; Ibn Kathir supports this syntax with a poetic example.
rows.anchor: {ويخرون} عطف صفة على صفة لا عطف سجود على سجود، كما قال الشاعر:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against polytheists who reject God's attribute of mercy and the name al-Rahman, the verse says either name invokes the same God, who possesses the most beautiful names.
rows.anchor: أي: لا فرق بين دعائكم له باسم "الله" أو باسم (3) " الرحمن "، فإنه ذو الأسماء الحسنى،

rows.speaker: مكحول
rows.claim: Mak-hul reports that a polytheist heard the Prophet invoke al-Rahman and al-Rahim in prostration, thought he was invoking two gods, and the verse was revealed; Ibn Jarir also transmits it from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: وقد روى مكحول (4) أن رجلا من المشركين سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يقول في سجوده: "يا رحمن يا رحيم"
